How records were built

One record is one documented occurrence: a decision, protest, incident or measured change tied to farmland conversion, water, power, housing or heritage around STSP campuses (Tainan, Kaohsiung, Ciaotou, Nanzih, Chiayi, Shalun, Pingtung).

Special districts (特定區). Records tagged 特定區 fall inside a special district plan, the urban-plan type drawn around a science park, HSR station or new town under the Urban Planning Act. Land in these districts is usually assembled by zone expropriation (區段徵收) or land readjustment (市地重劃) and then zoned residential, commercial or industrial; housing records here ask who that residential land actually serves.

Location. Filled symbols are sites named in the source. Hollow symbols sit on a district centroid when a source names only the district. Large dashed circles are regional (irrigation zones, multi-county droughts). Points sharing a centroid are nudged apart slightly.

Sources. Government releases, Taiwanese media (PTS, CNA, UDN, Liberty Times, Commercial Times and others) and Kollar (2025). Allegations and inferred dates are flagged in the record. Open the originals before citing; these summaries are a finding aid.

Basemap. District boundaries from taiwan-atlas (MOI data). Park markers are approximate locations, not footprints.
